positions.text: Naja and coauthors provide an independent qualification of Kaal’s claim that evidentiary records and a graph are complementary memory scales. Their peer-reviewed system links planned evidence to accountability traces and represents activities, outcomes, responsible agents, and their relationships in a single provenance-based knowledge graph for collection, inspection, query, and audit. That supports the record-to-review and graph-as-accumulated-accountability-information mechanisms. The article does not model reputation, condition future participation, or test the three-scale architecture together, so it qualifies two components rather than validating the full design.
scope_conditions: The response is limited to the four page-bound full-text passages and the one mapped Kaal claim.

External evidence level: peer-reviewed CC-BY IEEE Access article with a public 30-page repository PDF, clean machine-readable text, four exact page-bound passages, and Crossref, OpenAlex, and Semantic Scholar identity links.
Mapping review tier: independent substantive scholarly-growth qualification.
The article concerns AI-system accountability across design and implementation stages, not Kaal’s agentic-reputation substrate.
It supports the evidentiary-record-to-review and knowledge-graph preservation mechanisms but does not model reputation or condition future participation.
The evaluation compares information coverage with Datasheets, Model Cards, and FactSheets; it does not experimentally test the three memory scales as a joint architecture.
It does not test validation pools, staking, settlement, identity persistence, adversarial gaming, or live autonomous-agent behavior.
